newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai association says no finance firms in trouble.
newsitem.headline: Thai association says no finance firms in trouble.

text.p: Thailand's Association of Finance Companies said on Friday that stock market rumours that some finance firms may be hit by liquidity problems were groundless.

"Everybody knows that the Thai economy is not very good now but it does not mean that there are finance firms suffering from liquidity problems. We don't know where these rumours come and they are groundless," the association's manager, Chuleeporn Muamtanong. told Reuters.
The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index on Thursday closed down 13.81 points at 726.01 as investors sold on concerns over the renewed rumours about the finance companies.
Brokers said the index was expected to continue falling on Friday due to more investor jitters over the rumours.
Similar rumours have hit several finance firms in recent months amid talk their liquidity problems followed loan defaults by cash-strapped developers in the depressed property sector.
"Our association is worried about finance firms hit by these rumours. The association doesn't know how to prevent these kinds of rumours," said Chuleeporn.

But some market analysts continue to question the quality of loans extended to hard-hit property developers by financial institutions, particularly finance firms. There are also concerns about how well some finance firms may have provided for possible loan losses from the property sector.
